Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.

This study examined whether gut microbiome signatures associated with cognitive impairment in cirrhosis are consistent across patients from four countries (USA, Denmark, Lithuania, Mexico). Using stool shotgun metagenomics and PHES testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy, the authors identified taxonomic and functional microbial associations with cognitive scores that held across diverse dietary and clinical settings. The findings suggest a generalizable gut‒liver‒brain axis signature for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment.

iScience 2026-11-20 Medium

Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads.

DADEC is a new hybrid error-correction pipeline for noisy long reads that combines stringent de Bruijn graph correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive de Bruijn graph recovery in a confidence-ordered framework. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, it achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmarks while preserving genuine biological variation, avoiding the over-correction that plagues existing methods.

A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole.

This study characterizes the microbiome of a unique Caribbean marine sinkhole containing an acidic (pH ~6.25) and suboxic submerged lake at ~220 m depth, using multi-omics approaches on 59 size-filtered samples. The researchers resolved a specialized microbial community enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential, demonstrating how microbes adapt to extreme biogeochemical gradients that deviate strongly from standard oceanographic conditions.

Aerobic methane oxidation by microorganisms exacerbates neurotoxic methylmercury accumulation in rice paddy fields.

A large-scale field survey across China's rice-growing regions, combined with 13CH4-DNA stable isotope probing, reveals a positive association between aerobic methane oxidation and microbial mercury methylation in paddy soils. The findings suggest that microbes oxidizing methane also contribute to producing neurotoxic methylmercury, which then accumulates in rice, linking methane cycling to a major food-safety hazard.

PEONY: a global reference database of DNA viral (vOTU) sequences from viral size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes).

PEONY is an updated global reference database of DNA viral sequences (vOTUs, mostly dsDNA bacteriophages) derived exclusively from virus size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes). The update rebrands the previous database to reflect that it now contains only encapsidated viral sequences from viromes across global ecosystems, providing a cleaner reference for viral ecology and metagenomic studies.

Temperature effects on life history strategies for rapid growth potential of leaf epiphytic bacteria.

This study examined how temperature shapes the life-history strategies of leaf-dwelling (phyllosphere) bacteria across four alpine meadow plant species on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, combining an elevational gradient survey with a controlled warming experiment. The authors found that temperature is closely tied to the composition and assembly of epiphytic versus endophytic bacterial communities, with warming favoring rapid-growth life-history strategies. The work highlights the plant-atmosphere interface as a sensitive zone for microbial community shifts under climate warming.

Global Carriage of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Virulence Factors Among Physicians in Cirrhosis Care.

This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile the fecal microbiomes of 55 physicians caring for cirrhosis patients across 9 countries, examining carriage of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence factors (VFs). Physicians in low- and middle-income countries showed greater ARG diversity, which tracked with increased taxonomic richness, but overall carriage of clinically relevant ARGs and VFs was low regardless of country or patient exposure. The findings suggest that healthcare providers in cirrhosis care carry a modest resistance burden, with geographic income level shaping gut resistome diversity more than occupational exposure.
